p.src: The Kruskal picture gives an elegant description of the neighborhood of a Schwarzschild horizon, but a real black hole is not eternal: it forms when matter collapses. Which parts of the extended picture survive that physical history? To answer the question we need a diagram large enough to contain an entire spacetime and disciplined enough to preserve the motion of light. We will first compactify flat spacetime, then compactify Schwarzschild spacetime, and finally sew the appropriate pieces together across an infalling shell of radiation.

ja: クラスカル図はシュヴァルツシルト地平線の近傍を巧みに記述するが、現実のブラックホールは永遠に存在するわけではない。物質が崩壊するときに形成されるのである。拡張された図のどの部分が、その物理的な歴史を経てもなお生き残るのだろうか。この問いに答えるには、時空全体を収めるのに十分大きく、かつ光の運動を保つのに十分に統制された図が必要である。まず平坦な時空をコンパクト化し、次にシュヴァルツシルト時空をコンパクト化し、最後に落下する放射の殻を挟んで適切な部分同士を縫い合わせる。
zh: 克鲁斯卡尔图景为施瓦西视界附近区域提供了优雅的描述，但真实黑洞并非永恒存在：它是在物质坍缩时形成的。扩展图景中的哪些部分能在这一物理历史中保留下来？要回答这个问题，我们需要一幅足够大、能容纳整个时空，又足够严谨、能保持光之运动的图。我们将首先紧致化平直时空，然后紧致化施瓦西时空，最后将适当的部分跨越一个内落辐射壳层缝合起来。

p.src: This is already enough to say what a black hole does. In the exterior region $I$, objects and signals may go inward, but they may also remain outside or turn back out. In region $II$, by contrast, the causal verdict is fixed. Once one is in the interior, there is no future-directed causal path back to the exterior. To escape from region $II$ into either outside region would require a trajectory shallower than $45^\circ$ somewhere, and therefore faster than light. Every allowed future timelike trajectory ends on the singularity.

p.src: But the lecturer then insists on a second point, and it is the one that makes students uneasy. At that meeting event the shell passes its own Schwarzschild radius. Above that event, the horizon is the ordinary constant-radius horizon of the completed black hole.

zh: 但讲师随后坚持第二点，而正是这一点让学生们感到不安。视界并非仅仅在壳层穿过其自身施瓦西半径的那一刻出现，然后就固定不动。在放大的黑板图中，视界起初是靠近中心的一个微小 trapped region，向外扩展，穿过一部分仍然平坦的时空，直到后来才与入射壳层相遇。在那个相遇事件处，壳层穿过了它自己的施瓦西半径。在该事件之上，视界就是已形成黑洞的普通的恒定半径视界。

The shell has not yet arrived there, and it is not even visible on the observer’s past light cone. The observer feels no gravitational field and nevertheless cannot escape. The reason is not a local force. It is the global causal future of the event.

Alice may arrange in advance for Bob to send the shell and may therefore know what is coming before she sees it. Once her event is inside the horizon, however, neither a mirror nor an instruction can reach the required exterior point in time. p.src: Question from the audience: What happens to a mirror already inside the horizon, and is the singularity infinitely far in its future?

u.src: Question from the audience: What happens to a mirror already inside the horizon, and is the singularity infinitely far in its future?
en: Question from the audience: What happens to a mirror already inside the horizon, and is the singularity infinitely far in its future?
ja: 受講者からの質問: すでに事象の地平面の内側にある鏡はどうなるのか、また特異点はその未来において無限に遠いのか。
zh: 听众提问: 对于已经位于视界内部的镜子会发生什么？奇点是否在其未来无限远处？

p.src: Response: The mirror is simply another doomed object. It may reflect the light locally, but the reflected light, the mirror, and Alice all end on the singularity. A generic infalling worldline reaches it in finite proper time. Only the ideal upper corner of the compactified diagram is infinitely far away. Trying to remain near that corner would require unbounded acceleration and energy; moreover, between fixed events an accelerated clock accumulates less proper time than an inertial one, not more.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:08:19–01:10:19)

ja: 回答: その鏡は、単に別の運命づけられた物体にすぎない。鏡は光を局所的に反射しうるが、反射された光も、鏡も、アリスも、すべて特異点で終わる。一般的な落下世界線は有限の固有時間でそこに到達する。無限に遠いのは、コンパクト化された図の理想的な上端の角だけである。その角の近くにとどまろうとすれば、無限の加速度とエネルギーが必要になる。さらに、固定された事象間では、加速された時計は慣性の時計よりも多くの固有時間を蓄積するのではなく、少ない固有時間しか蓄積しない。  (講義時刻: 01:08:19–01:10:19)
zh: 回答: 镜子不过是另一个注定毁灭的物体。它可以在局部反射光，但被反射的光、镜子以及Alice最终都终结于奇点。一条一般的下落世界线在有限的固有时内到达奇点。只有紧致化图中理想的上角才是无限远的。试图停留在那个角附近将需要无界的加速度和能量；此外，在固定事件之间，加速的时钟积累的固有时比惯性时钟更少，而不是更多。  (讲课时间: 01:08:19–01:10:19)

p.src: An instant of time in curved spacetime means a chosen spacelike hypersurface. A stack of such surfaces is a foliation, and assigning a number to each surface defines a time coordinate. Different foliations cut the same collapse diagram differently. They disagree about which distant events are simultaneous, but they do not change which null rays reach infinity.

ja: 曲がった時空における時間の瞬間とは、選ばれた空間的超曲面を意味する。そのような曲面を積み重ねたものが葉層であり、各曲面に数を割り当てることで時間座標が定義される。異なる葉層は同じ崩壊図を異なる仕方で切る。それらはどの遠方の事象が同時であるかについては一致しないが、どのヌル光線が無限遠に到達するかは変えない。

ja: 受講者からの質問: 最終的なシュヴァルツシルト半径の半分の位置に最初にいる観測者はどうなるのか。その観測者は殻が到着したときにのみ重力を感じるべきではないのか。

p.src: Response: Exactly. The observer first crosses the growing event horizon while still in flat spacetime and feels no sudden force. The infalling radiation shell is material and may later be felt; the event horizon is not. Crossing it means only that every future-directed causal path now fails to reach infinity. In that precise sense the horizon is ghostly.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:16:17–01:17:45)

ja: 回答: そのとおりである。その観測者は、依然として平坦な時空にいるうちに、成長する事象の地平面を最初に横切るが、突然の力を感じることはない。落下する放射殻は物質であり、後に感じられるかもしれないが、事象の地平面はそうではない。それを横切るということは、未来向きの因果的経路がすべて今や無限遠に到達しないということを意味するにすぎない。まさにその意味で、地平面は幽霊のようなものである。  (講義時刻: 01:16:17–01:17:45)
zh: 回答: 正是如此。观察者首先在仍处于平坦时空时越过增长的视界，感受不到突然的力。下落的辐射壳层是物质性的，之后可能被感受到；事件视界则不是。越过它只意味着现在每一条未来指向的因果路径都无法到达无穷远。正是在这个精确的意义上，视界是幽灵般的。  (讲课时间: 01:16:17–01:17:45)

p.src: What the Diagram Preserves

u.src: What the Diagram Preserves
en: What the Diagram Preserves
ja: 図が保存するもの
zh: 图所保留的内容

p.src: The shapes on the page must not be read as a scale drawing. A small corner may represent an infinite region of spacetime, while a large patch may represent a modest physical interval. Compactification deliberately sacrifices metric size in order to preserve null directions. What survives is cause and effect: who can send a signal to whom, which events can influence which others, and which worldlines are trapped by the speed-of-light limit.

p.src: Question from the audience: If the picture distorts lengths and times so severely, what does it represent faithfully?

u.src: Question from the audience: If the picture distorts lengths and times so severely, what does it represent faithfully?
en: Question from the audience: If the picture distorts lengths and times so severely, what does it represent faithfully?
ja: 受講者からの質問: この図が長さと時間をそれほどひどく歪めるなら、それは何を忠実に表しているのか。
zh: 听众提问: 如果这幅图如此严重地扭曲了长度和时间，那么它忠实地表示了什么？

p.src: Response: It represents light rays and therefore causal structure. To locate the event horizon, trace the last outgoing null ray backward from future infinity. Trying to infer the answer from apparent distances on the page is unreliable. Once the causal diagram is drawn, questions about signals, escape, and no-return have geometric answers even though the metric scale has been suppressed.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:18:56–01:21:45)

p.src: Question from the audience: How long does it take to become comfortable enough with Penrose diagrams to use them intuitively?

u.src: Question from the audience: How long does it take to become comfortable enough with Penrose diagrams to use them intuitively?
en: Question from the audience: How long does it take to become comfortable enough with Penrose diagrams to use them intuitively?
ja: 受講者からの質問: ペンローズ図を直観的に使えるようになるには、どれくらい慣れる必要があるのか。
zh: 听众提问: 要熟练到能凭直觉使用彭罗斯图，需要多长时间？

p.src: Response: Not long. The practical prescription is to draw them, trace null lines, and test possible worldlines until the causal restrictions become familiar. Intuition here is acquired by working with the diagrams, not by guessing without them.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:21:49–01:22:05)

u.src: Response: Not long. The practical prescription is to draw them, trace null lines, and test possible worldlines until the causal restrictions become familiar. Intuition here is acquired by working with the diagrams, not by guessing without them.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:21:49–01:22:05)

zh: 听众提问: 这种视觉方法是否与量子力学相反？在量子力学中，数学往往比图像更可靠。

p.src: Response: To a considerable extent, yes. General relativity is classical physics. Four-dimensional curved spacetime is difficult to picture literally, and a Penrose diagram is still abstract, but its causal geometry can be drawn and explored much further than the underlying reality of quantum mechanics can. That difference is part of what makes these diagrams so powerful.  (Lecture timestamp: 01:22:05–01:22:58)
